sentences.text: Thereafter, petitioner had filed bail application before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc. No.1095/2024 which came to be rejected on 10th January 2025.
Therefore, petitioner is before this Court.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner has reiterated the grounds urged in the petition.
7. Learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the petition.
Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submits that he has no objection to grant the regular bail to the petitioner and submits that petitioner and victim are married.

9. Perusal of the material on record would go to show that based on the first information submitted by the respondent No.2 FIR was registered against the petitioner in Crime No.84/2024 by the Kanakapura Rural Police Station, Kanakapura Circle, Ramanagara District.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 10. During the course of investigation, petitioner was arrested on 07.08.2024 and subsequently, was remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.

11. Statement of the victim under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded on 05.06.2024 and in the said statement, victim has stated that she is aged about 18 years and she is in love with the petitioner.

She has stated that since her mother did not agree to perform her marriage with the petitioner, she had left the house on 16.04.2023 and met the petitioner and thereafter, she married the petitioner in a temple NC: 2025:KHC:10243 at Dyapegowdanadoddi, Kanakapura.
Subsequently, she started residing with the petitioner in his house and parents of the petitioner had accepted their marriage.
Since the victim was pregnant, she had gone to the Primary Health Centre and respondent No.2 has thereafter filed the police complaint.
12. The victim girl has not made any serious allegations against the petitioner which would prima facie attract the offences alleged against the petitioner.
On the other hand, victim girl has stated that she is now married to the petitioner.
13. Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the matter, petitioner's prayer needs to be granted.

14. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.84 of 2024, Kanakapura Rural Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code, Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, and NC: 2025:KHC:10243 Sections 9 and 11 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, subject to the following conditions:
